subject: combined-science

items.q: Two plants grown from cuttings of the same parent plant are given different amounts of light. One grows much taller than the other. What does this difference show?
items.correct: The environment has influenced the phenotype of the plants
items.misconception: The plants inherited different genes for their height
items.why: Inheritance is taught before variation, and characteristics are described as being 'passed on', so students treat genes as the only possible source of a difference and overlook the conditions in which an organism developed. Variation may be due to the genes they have inherited (genetic causes), the conditions in which they have developed (environmental causes), or a combination of genes and the environment; the genome and its interaction with the environment influence the development of the phenotype.
items.random_wrong: The change in light has caused a mutation in one plant

items.q: Which of these describes the causes of variation between individuals in a population?
items.correct: Inherited genes, the conditions of development, or both
items.misconception: Inherited genes alone, which are passed on by the parents
items.why: Inheritance is taught before variation, and characteristics are described as being 'passed on', so students treat genes as the only possible source of a difference and overlook the conditions in which an organism developed. Variation may be due to the genes they have inherited (genetic causes), the conditions in which they have developed (environmental causes), or a combination of genes and the environment; the genome and its interaction with the environment influence the development of the phenotype.
items.random_wrong: Mutations that are produced by a change in the environment

items.q: All variants arise from mutations. Which statement about mutations and phenotype is correct?
items.correct: Most mutations have no effect on the phenotype
items.misconception: Most mutations lead to a change in the phenotype
items.why: Mutations are usually introduced through striking examples in which an organism is visibly changed, so students assume that any change in the DNA must show up in the organism. All variants arise from mutations, but most have no effect on the phenotype, some influence phenotype and very few determine phenotype.
items.random_wrong: Mutations happen only when the environment changes

items.q: A mutation produces a new phenotype in a population. The environment then changes, and the new phenotype is suited to the new conditions. What is the likely result?
items.correct: A relatively rapid change in the species can take place
items.misconception: More mutations of this type occur in the population
items.why: Examples always pair a new phenotype with an environmental change, so students read the environmental change as the cause of the mutation rather than as the thing that makes the new phenotype useful. Mutations occur continuously. Very rarely a mutation will lead to a new phenotype, and if the new phenotype is suited to an environmental change it can lead to a relatively rapid change in the species.
items.random_wrong: Each organism changes to the new phenotype in its lifetime

items.correct: A change in the inherited characteristics of a population over time
items.misconception: A change in the characteristics of an animal during its lifetime
items.why: In everyday speech 'evolve' simply means 'gradually change', so students picture one animal changing rather than the inherited characteristics of a whole population changing across generations. Evolution is a change in the inherited characteristics of a population over time through a process of natural selection which may result in the formation of a new species.
items.random_wrong: A change in appearance that makes a population a new species

items.q: In a beetle population most beetles are pale and a few are dark. The tree bark the beetles live on becomes darker, so birds find the pale beetles more easily. After many generations most of the beetles are dark. Which statement explains this?
items.correct: Dark beetles survived to breed and passed on their variant
items.misconception: The beetles developed a darker colour because they needed it
items.why: Purpose-driven language such as 'the animal needed a thicker coat' is common in everyday explanations, and it is easier to imagine an organism responding to a problem than to imagine that variation was already there. Evolution occurs through natural selection of variants that give rise to phenotypes best suited to their environment, and all variants arise from mutations, which occur continuously.
items.random_wrong: Each pale beetle became darker as the tree bark grew darker

items.q: Two populations of one species have been separated for a very long time and now look very different. What must be shown before they are classed as two new species?
items.correct: That they can no longer produce fertile offspring together
items.misconception: That their phenotypes are different enough to tell apart
items.why: Species are usually met as named pictures in a key, so appearance becomes the test students apply, and the breeding test is rarely used in earlier work. If two populations of one species become so different in phenotype that they can no longer interbreed to produce fertile offspring they have formed two new species.
items.random_wrong: That each population has developed the features that it needs

items.q: A farmer chooses the cows that produce the most milk and breeds them together. From their offspring he again breeds those that produce the most milk, and he repeats this for many generations. Which statement about this process is correct?
items.correct: It is selective breeding, as the farmer chose the parents
items.misconception: It is natural selection, as the best cows survive and breed
items.why: Natural selection and selective breeding are taught together and both end with a population showing a characteristic, so the human choice of parents is forgotten. Selective breeding (artificial selection) is the process by which humans breed plants and animals for particular genetic characteristics, choosing parents with the desired characteristic from a mixed population.
items.random_wrong: It is genetic engineering, as the genome is being modified

items.q: Which statement about selective breeding is correct?
items.correct: It can lead to inbreeding in the breeds it produces
items.misconception: It removes inherited defects from the breeds produced
items.why: Selective breeding is introduced through its successes, such as more milk, more meat and disease resistance in crops, so students assume the process removes anything harmful. Selective breeding can lead to 'inbreeding' where some breeds are particularly prone to disease or inherited defects.
items.random_wrong: It happens in the wild without human choice

items.correct: A gene is transferred into the cells of another organism
items.misconception: Parents with the desired characteristic are bred together
items.why: Both processes are presented as ways of obtaining a desired characteristic, and 'engineering the genes' sounds to students like choosing which genes are passed on. Genetic engineering is a process which involves modifying the genome of an organism by introducing a gene from another organism to give a desired characteristic.
items.random_wrong: Cells from one organism are grown into identical copies

items.q: Which statement about the uses of genetic engineering is correct?
items.correct: Bacterial cells have been genetically engineered to make human insulin
items.misconception: Tissue culture is used to add genes to bacterial cells
items.why: Both processes appear in the same part of the course and both are pictured as laboratory work on cells, so students merge them into one idea of 'making organisms artificially'. Genetic engineering modifies the genome of an organism by introducing a gene from another organism, whereas tissue culture uses small groups of cells from part of a plant to grow identical new plants.
items.random_wrong: Inherited disorders are now cured using genetic modification

items.q: Which statement about genetically modified (GM) crops is correct?
items.correct: GM crops may affect wild flower and insect populations
items.misconception: GM crops generally produce lower yields than other food crops
items.why: Students know that GM crops are controversial and assume the objection must be that they do not work, rather than a concern about wild populations or about human health. GM crops generally show increased yields. Concerns about GM crops include the effect on populations of wild flowers and insects, and some people feel the effects of eating GM crops on human health have not been fully explored.
items.random_wrong: GM crops are grown from cells taken from one parent plant

items.q: Which statement describes the main steps in the process of genetic engineering?
items.correct: Enzymes isolate the gene, which a vector puts into cells
items.misconception: Enzymes cut out the gene and carry it into the cells
items.why: Enzymes are the first thing named in the process and are remembered as 'the tool that does the job', so the separate vector step is left out. Enzymes are used to isolate the required gene; this gene is inserted into a vector, usually a bacterial plasmid or a virus; the vector is used to insert the gene into the required cells.
items.random_wrong: Cells are taken from an organism and grown into copies

items.q: How long does selective breeding take before all the offspring show the desired characteristic?
items.correct: Many generations of choosing and breeding.
items.misconception: Breeding the two chosen parents once produces offspring that all show the desired characteristic.
items.why: Written answers often describe a single round of breeding, and students forget that the offspring still vary so the choosing and breeding has to be repeated. From the offspring those with the desired characteristic are bred together. This continues over many generations until all the offspring show the desired characteristic.
items.note: no MCQ covers this misconception, so no third distractor was authored for it; none invented

items.q: How is genetic modification used at present for inherited disorders?
items.correct: Modern medical research is exploring the possibility of using it to overcome some inherited disorders.
items.misconception: Genetic modification is already a routine treatment that cures inherited disorders in patients.
items.why: News reports about changing genes describe cures, and students do not separate research that is exploring a possibility from treatment that is in routine use. Modern medical research is exploring the possibility of genetic modification to overcome some inherited disorders.
items.note: no MCQ covers this misconception, so no third distractor was authored for it; none invented
